title: Isaiah 1 — Hear, O skies: the rebellious children, the worthless offerings, and the faithful city

verdicts.reasoning: Re-read: ḥăzôn … ʾăšer ḥāzāh, four royal names, standard superscription; line exact, not disputed.

Re-parsed šimʿû (Qal impv mp) / haʾăzînî (Hiphil impv fs to ʾereṣ), giddaltî wᵉrômamtî (Piel/Polel 1cs). 'skies' follows central shamayim (direct) and is a standard sense of šāmayim; 'rebelled against me' for pāšʿû bî matches ASV/NRSV/NJPS.
qōnēhû 'its owner', ʾēḇûs bᵉʿālāyw 'its master's crib' (plural of majesty bᵉʿālîm read as singular owner), hiṯbônān 'understand'; standard, not disputed.

citations: Westermann, Basic Forms of Prophetic Speech (1967)

citations: BDB s.v. מָה (ʿal-meh 'upon what ground? wherefore?')

MT kᵉmahpēḵaṯ zārîm kept per mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah; the sᵉḏōm conjecture is properly disclosed as having no manuscript support. ʾarṣᵉḵem / ʾaḏmaṯḵem distinguished as land / ground per central entries.
nôṯᵉrāh Niphal pf 3fs; sukkāh / mᵉlûnāh / miqšāh standard. 'besieged' for nᵉṣûrāh (Qal pass. ptc of nṣr, or by some derived from ṣwr) is the ASV/NRSV reading and the commentary states the derivation.

Verified the athnach on כִּמְעָ֑ט in the WLC source: the accents join kimʿāṭ to the remnant clause, so 'a very small remnant' follows MT; the alternative division is disclosed. Non-application of central she-erit to śārîḏ is correct.
dᵉḇar-YHWH // tôraṯ ʾĕlōhênû; 'teaching' per signed-off overlay torah-teaching-isaiah, 'our God' per elohai-elohenu entry. qᵉṣînê sᵉḏōm 'rulers of Sodom' standard.
lāmmāh-lî 'What to me', yōʾmar (impf, 'says'), mᵉrîʾîm 'fed beasts', ʿattûḏîm 'he-goats'; cultic terms per central qorbanot / olah (direct). Not disputed.
lērāʾôṯ is pointed as Niphal infinitive with syncopated he; 'to appear before me' follows the vowels and the Qal 'see my face' alternative is disclosed. Consistent with the MT policy.

lōʾ tôsîp̄û hāḇîʾ 'Bring no more'; minḥaṯ-šāwʾ 'worthless meal-offerings' (cultic-list clause of central qorbanot); ʾāwen waʿăṣārāh kept as MT with the LXX nēsteian disclosed. Accent division (zaqef on šāwʾ, athnach on lî) supports the line's clause break.

raḥăṣû, hizzakkû (Hithpael of zkh with assimilated t), hāsîrû rōaʿ maʿallᵉlêḵem, ḥiḏlû hārēaʿ; standard.

verdicts.reasoning: Re-read the WLC pointing: וּפֹעֲלוֹ has holem on pe and hatef patah on ayin, the shape of the suffixed Qal participle pōʿēl; the noun pōʿal with 3ms suffix is pointed pāʿŏlô (Jer 22:13; Prov 20:11). The MT therefore points 'its maker', and 'his work' is a re-vocalisation. Since the book translates the pointed MT (as at 1:12), revise the line to: 'And the strong shall become tinder, and its maker a spark; and both of them shall burn together, with none to quench them.' Move 'his work' (ASV, NRSV, on the repointing pāʿŏlô) into commentary. The reviewer did not page-verify how BDB/HALOT classify this site.

paragraphs.text: חֲזוֹן֙ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֣הוּ בֶן־אָמ֔וֹץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה עַל־יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם בִּימֵ֨י עֻזִּיָּ֧הוּ יוֹתָ֛ם אָחָ֥ז יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ מַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃

i18n.en: The vision of Isaiah son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
i18n.he: חֲזוֹן֙ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֣הוּ בֶן־אָמ֔וֹץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה עַל־יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם בִּימֵ֨י עֻזִּיָּ֧הוּ יוֹתָ֛ם אָחָ֥ז יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ מַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃

notes.official: *ḥăzôn yᵉšaʿyāhû* “The vision of Isaiah” is the superscription of the whole book, not only of chapter 1. *ḥāzôn* names prophetic revelation as something “seen” (*ʾăšer ḥāzāh* “which he saw”), even where what follows is spoken oracle. The four kings date Isaiah’s activity to the second half of the eighth century BCE (Wildberger, *Isaiah 1–12*, Continental Commentary 1991; Blenkinsopp, *Isaiah 1–39*, AB 19, 2000).

paragraphs.translit: ḥăzōn yəšaʿyāhū ben-ʾāmōṣ ʾăšer ḥāzāh ʿal-yəhūdāh wīrūšālim bīmē ʿuzziyyāhū yōtām ʾāḥāz yəḥizqiyyāhū malkē yəhūdāh

paragraphs.text: שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמַ֙יִם֙ וְהַאֲזִ֣ינִי אֶ֔רֶץ כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּ֑ר בָּנִים֙ גִּדַּ֣לְתִּי וְרוֹמַ֔מְתִּי וְהֵ֖ם פָּ֥שְׁעוּ בִֽי׃

i18n.en: Hear, O skies, and give ear, O earth, for YHWH has spoken: Children I have reared and brought up, but they have rebelled against me.
i18n.he: שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמַ֙יִם֙ וְהַאֲזִ֣ינִי אֶ֔רֶץ כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּ֑ר בָּנִים֙ גִּדַּ֣לְתִּי וְרוֹמַ֔מְתִּי וְהֵ֖ם פָּ֥שְׁעוּ בִֽי׃

notes.official: *šimʿû šāmayim wᵉhaʾăzînî ʾereṣ* “Hear, O skies, and give ear, O earth”: the two halves of the cosmos are called as witnesses, as in Deut 32:1, and the chapter is commonly read as a covenant lawsuit (*rîḇ*) against Israel (Huffmon, “The Covenant Lawsuit in the Prophets,” *JBL* 78, 1959). *šāmayim* is “skies” under the central `shamayim` entry; *ʾereṣ*, paired with the skies, is “earth” under the cosmic clause of the central `eretz` entry. *pāšʿû bî* is “they have rebelled against me” (ASV, NRSV, NJPS). The same construction is “transgressed against me” at 43:27; here the parent-and-children frame of the verse makes “rebelled” the natural English (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-1`).

paragraphs.translit: šimʿū šāmayim wəhaʾăzīnī ʾereṣ kī YHWH dibbēr bānīm giddaltī wərōmamtī wəhēm pāšəʿū bī

paragraphs.text: יָדַ֥ע שׁוֹר֙ קֹנֵ֔הוּ וַחֲמ֖וֹר אֵב֣וּס בְּעָלָ֑יו יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔ע עַמִּ֖י לֹ֥א הִתְבּוֹנָֽן׃

i18n.en: The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master's crib; Israel does not know, my people does not understand.
i18n.he: יָדַ֥ע שׁוֹר֙ קֹנֵ֔הוּ וַחֲמ֖וֹר אֵב֣וּס בְּעָלָ֑יו יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔ע עַמִּ֖י לֹ֥א הִתְבּוֹנָֽן׃

paragraphs.translit: yādaʿ šōr qōnēhū waḥămōr ʾēbūs bəʿālāyw yiśrāʾēl lōʾ yādaʿ ʿammī lōʾ hitbōnān

paragraphs.text: ה֣וֹי ׀ גּ֣וֹי חֹטֵ֗א עַ֚ם כֶּ֣בֶד עָוֺ֔ן זֶ֣רַע מְרֵעִ֔ים בָּנִ֖ים מַשְׁחִיתִ֑ים עָזְב֣וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֗ה נִֽאֲצ֛וּ אֶת־קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נָזֹ֥רוּ אָחֽוֹר׃

i18n.en: Woe, sinful nation, a people heavy with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children who deal corruptly! They have forsaken YHWH, they have spurned the Holy One of Israel, they have turned away backward.
i18n.he: ה֣וֹי ׀ גּ֣וֹי חֹטֵ֗א עַ֚ם כֶּ֣בֶד עָוֺ֔ן זֶ֣רַע מְרֵעִ֔ים בָּנִ֖ים מַשְׁחִיתִ֑ים עָזְב֣וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֗ה נִֽאֲצ֛וּ אֶת־קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נָזֹ֥רוּ אָחֽוֹר׃

notes.official: *hôy* is rendered “Woe” under the book-level ruling (overlay `hoy-woe-isaiah`), as at 29:1, 15 and 45:9, 10; ASV, NRSV and NJPS have “Ah” here. The cry is the opening of a funeral lament, turned against the living nation (Wildberger; Westermann, *Basic Forms of Prophetic Speech*, 1967). *qᵉḏôš yiśrāʾēl* “the Holy One of Israel” appears here for the first time: it is the characteristic divine title of the book, used in both its halves. *ʿăwōn* “iniquity” follows the central `avon-iniquity-cross-corpus-keyword` entry.

paragraphs.translit: hōy | gōy ḥōṭēʾ ʿam kebed ʿāwn zeraʿ mərēʿīm bānīm mašḥītīm ʿāzəbū ʾet-YHWH niʾăṣū ʾet-qədōš yiśrāʾēl nāzōrū ʾāḥōr

paragraphs.text: עַ֣ל מֶ֥ה תֻכּ֛וּ ע֖וֹד תּוֹסִ֣יפוּ סָרָ֑ה כָּל־רֹ֣אשׁ לָחֳלִ֔י וְכָל־לֵבָ֖ב דַּוָּֽי׃

i18n.en: Why will you still be struck, that you continue in revolt? The whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint.
i18n.he: עַ֣ל מֶ֥ה תֻכּ֛וּ ע֖וֹד תּוֹסִ֣יפוּ סָרָ֑ה כָּל־רֹ֣אשׁ לָחֳלִ֔י וְכָל־לֵבָ֖ב דַּוָּֽי׃

notes.official: *ʿal meh tukkû ʿôḏ* “Why will you still be struck” follows ASV, NRSV and NJPS, and BDB, which gives *ʿal-meh* the sense “wherefore.” Some commentators take *ʿal meh* as “on what (part)?”, so that the question begins the image of the beaten body completed in v. 6 (“the whole head … from the sole of the foot even to the head”). The line keeps the usual sense; the body image is carried by the second half of the verse in either reading (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-1`).

paragraphs.translit: ʿal meh tukkū ʿōd tōsīpū sārāh kol-rōʾš loḥŏlī wəkol-lēbāb dawwāy

paragraphs.text: מִכַּף־רֶ֤גֶל וְעַד־רֹאשׁ֙ אֵֽין־בּ֣וֹ מְתֹ֔ם פֶּ֥צַע וְחַבּוּרָ֖ה וּמַכָּ֣ה טְרִיָּ֑ה לֹא־זֹ֙רוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א חֻבָּ֔שׁוּ וְלֹ֥א רֻכְּכָ֖ה בַּשָּֽׁמֶן׃

i18n.en: From the sole of the foot even to the head there is no soundness in it — wounds and bruises and fresh blows; they have not been pressed out, nor bound up, nor softened with oil.
i18n.he: מִכַּף־רֶ֤גֶל וְעַד־רֹאשׁ֙ אֵֽין־בּ֣וֹ מְתֹ֔ם פֶּ֥צַע וְחַבּוּרָ֖ה וּמַכָּ֣ה טְרִיָּ֑ה לֹא־זֹ֙רוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א חֻבָּ֔שׁוּ וְלֹ֥א רֻכְּכָ֖ה בַּשָּֽׁמֶן׃

paragraphs.translit: mikkap-regel wəʿad-rōʾš ʾēn-bō mətōm peṣaʿ wəḥabbūrāh ūmakkāh ṭəriyyāh lōʾ-zōrū wəlōʾ ḥubbāšū wəlōʾ rukkəkāh baššāmen

paragraphs.text: אַרְצְכֶ֣ם שְׁמָמָ֔ה עָרֵיכֶ֖ם שְׂרֻפ֣וֹת אֵ֑שׁ אַדְמַתְכֶ֗ם לְנֶגְדְּכֶם֙ זָרִים֙ אֹכְלִ֣ים אֹתָ֔הּ וּשְׁמָמָ֖ה כְּמַהְפֵּכַ֥ת זָרִֽים׃

i18n.en: Your land is a desolation; your cities are burned with fire; your ground — before your eyes strangers devour it; and it is a desolation, like an overthrow by strangers.
i18n.he: אַרְצְכֶ֣ם שְׁמָמָ֔ה עָרֵיכֶ֖ם שְׂרֻפ֣וֹת אֵ֑שׁ אַדְמַתְכֶ֗ם לְנֶגְדְּכֶם֙ זָרִים֙ אֹכְלִ֣ים אֹתָ֔הּ וּשְׁמָמָ֖ה כְּמַהְפֵּכַ֥ת זָרִֽים׃

notes.official: *kᵉmahpēḵaṯ zārîm* “like an overthrow by strangers” is the Masoretic Text, and the line keeps it (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). The noun *mahpēḵāh* is otherwise used only of the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah (Deut 29:22; Amos 4:11; Isa 13:19; Jer 49:18; 50:40), and Sodom and Gomorrah are named in vv. 9–10. For that reason many commentators, and the apparatus of BHS, emend the second *zārîm* to *sᵉḏōm*, “like the overthrow of Sodom” (Wildberger). No Hebrew manuscript or ancient version attests the emended text. The formula is recorded under the central `mahapekhah-overthrowing-formula` entry. *ʾaḏmaṯḵem* “your ground” follows the central `adam-adamah` entry, and *ʾarṣᵉḵem* “your land” the territorial sense of central `eretz`.

paragraphs.translit: ʾarṣəkem šəmāmāh ʿārēkem śərupōt ʾēš ʾadmatkem lənegdəkem zārīm ʾōkəlīm ʾōtāh ūšəmāmāh kəmahpēkat zārīm

paragraphs.text: וְנוֹתְרָ֥ה בַת־צִיּ֖וֹן כְּסֻכָּ֣ה בְכָ֑רֶם כִּמְלוּנָ֥ה בְמִקְשָׁ֖ה כְּעִ֥יר נְצוּרָֽה׃

i18n.en: And the daughter of Zion is left like a booth in a vineyard, like a hut in a cucumber field, like a besieged city.
i18n.he: וְנוֹתְרָ֥ה בַת־צִיּ֖וֹן כְּסֻכָּ֣ה בְכָ֑רֶם כִּמְלוּנָ֥ה בְמִקְשָׁ֖ה כְּעִ֥יר נְצוּרָֽה׃

notes.official: *bat-ṣiyyôn* “the daughter of Zion” keeps the corpus wording (Micah, Zephaniah, Lamentations). The construction is appositional: the daughter who is Zion, the city personified as a young woman, which NRSV renders “daughter Zion.” *kᵉʿîr nᵉṣûrāh* “like a besieged city” (ASV, NRSV): the participle is from *nṣr* “watch, guard,” which can mean to watch a city in order to blockade it (Jer 4:16 *nōṣᵉrîm* “watchers,” that is, besiegers). The watchman’s booth and the hut of the preceding similes suggest the same root. NJPS “a city beleaguered” agrees (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-1`).

paragraphs.translit: wənōtərāh bat-ṣiyyōn kəsukkāh bəkārem kimlūnāh bəmiqšāh kəʿīr nəṣūrāh

paragraphs.text: לוּלֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הוֹתִ֥יר לָ֛נוּ שָׂרִ֖יד כִּמְעָ֑ט כִּסְדֹ֣ם הָיִ֔ינוּ לַעֲמֹרָ֖ה דָּמִֽינוּ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Had not YHWH of hosts left us a very small remnant, we would have been like Sodom, we would have resembled Gomorrah.
i18n.he: לוּלֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הוֹתִ֥יר לָ֛נוּ שָׂרִ֖יד כִּמְעָ֑ט כִּסְדֹ֣ם הָיִ֔ינוּ לַעֲמֹרָ֖ה דָּמִֽינוּ׃ (ס)

notes.official: *hôṯîr lānû śārîḏ kimʿāṭ* “left us a very small remnant”: the Masoretic accents (athnach on *kimʿāṭ*) join “a little” to the remnant, as ASV does. Several versions join it to the next clause: “we would almost have been like Sodom.” *śārîḏ* is the survivor of a disaster. It is not the remnant-keyword *šᵉʾār* / *šᵉʾērîṯ* of 10:20–22, so the central `she-erit-remnant-cross-corpus-theological-keyword` entry is not applied. The LXX has *sperma* “seed,” the form Paul quotes at Rom 9:29 (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-1`). “YHWH of hosts” follows overlay `yhwh-tzevaot-hosts-isaiah`.

paragraphs.translit: lūlē YHWH ṣəbāʾōt hōtīr lānū śārīd kimʿāṭ kisdōm hāyīnū laʿămōrāh dāmīnū (s)

paragraphs.text: שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה קְצִינֵ֣י סְדֹ֑ם הַאֲזִ֛ינוּ תּוֹרַ֥ת אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ עַ֥ם עֲמֹרָֽה׃

i18n.en: Hear the word of YHWH, you rulers of Sodom; give ear to the teaching of our God, you people of Gomorrah.
i18n.he: שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה קְצִינֵ֣י סְדֹ֑ם הַאֲזִ֛ינוּ תּוֹרַ֥ת אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ עַ֥ם עֲמֹרָֽה׃

notes.official: *tôraṯ ʾĕlōhênû* “the teaching of our God” stands parallel to *dᵉḇar-YHWH* “the word of YHWH”: the prophet’s own instruction, not a written law-code. *tôrāh* is “teaching” under overlay `torah-teaching-isaiah` (ASV “law”; NJPS “instruction”), and “our God” follows overlay `elohai-elohenu-doxology-isaiah-25`. The leaders of Jerusalem are addressed as “rulers of Sodom” and “people of Gomorrah,” taking up the comparison of v. 9.

paragraphs.translit: šimʿū dəbar-YHWH qəṣīnē sədōm haʾăzīnū tōrat ʾĕlōhēnū ʿam ʿămōrāh

paragraphs.text: לָמָּה־לִּ֤י רֹב־זִבְחֵיכֶם֙ יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שָׂבַ֛עְתִּי עֹל֥וֹת אֵילִ֖ים וְחֵ֣לֶב מְרִיאִ֑ים וְדַ֨ם פָּרִ֧ים וּכְבָשִׂ֛ים וְעַתּוּדִ֖ים לֹ֥א חָפָֽצְתִּי׃

i18n.en: What to me is the multitude of your sacrifices? says YHWH. I have had my fill of burnt-offerings of rams and the fat of fed beasts; and in the blood of bulls and lambs and he-goats I take no delight.
i18n.he: לָמָּה־לִּ֤י רֹב־זִבְחֵיכֶם֙ יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שָׂבַ֛עְתִּי עֹל֥וֹת אֵילִ֖ים וְחֵ֣לֶב מְרִיאִ֑ים וְדַ֨ם פָּרִ֧ים וּכְבָשִׂ֛ים וְעַתּוּדִ֖ים לֹ֥א חָפָֽצְתִּי׃

notes.official: The verse opens the list of cultic acts in vv. 11–15: *zᵉḇāḥîm* “sacrifices,” *ʿōlôṯ* “burnt-offerings,” the fat and the blood. The terms follow the central `qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus` and `olah-burnt-offering` entries. The rejection of sacrifice offered without justice is shared with Amos 5:21–24, Hos 6:6 and Mic 6:6–8.

paragraphs.translit: lāmmāh-lī rōb-zibḥēkem yōʾmar YHWH śābaʿtī ʿōlōt ʾēlīm wəḥēleb mərīʾīm wədam pārīm ūkəbāśīm wəʿattūdīm lōʾ ḥāpāṣəttī

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י תָבֹ֔אוּ לֵרָא֖וֹת פָּנָ֑י מִי־בִקֵּ֥שׁ זֹ֛את מִיֶּדְכֶ֖ם רְמֹ֥ס חֲצֵרָֽי׃

i18n.en: When you come to appear before me, who has required this from your hand, to trample my courts?
i18n.he: כִּ֣י תָבֹ֔אוּ לֵרָא֖וֹת פָּנָ֑י מִי־בִקֵּ֥שׁ זֹ֛את מִיֶּדְכֶ֖ם רְמֹ֥ס חֲצֵרָֽי׃

notes.official: *lērāʾôṯ pānāy* “to appear before me” follows the Masoretic vowels, a Niphal infinitive with the *he* elided (GKC §51l). The same pointing occurs in the pilgrimage laws (Exod 23:15; 34:20, 24; Deut 16:16). Many scholars hold that the consonants were first read as the Qal, “to see my face,” and that the vowels were changed to avoid speaking of seeing God. The line keeps the pointed text (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

paragraphs.translit: kī tābōʾū lērāʾōt pānāy mī-biqqēš zōʾt miyyedkem rəmōs ḥăṣērāy

paragraphs.text: לֹ֣א תוֹסִ֗יפוּ הָבִיא֙ מִנְחַת־שָׁ֔וְא קְטֹ֧רֶת תּוֹעֵבָ֛ה הִ֖יא לִ֑י חֹ֤דֶשׁ וְשַׁבָּת֙ קְרֹ֣א מִקְרָ֔א לֹא־אוּכַ֥ל אָ֖וֶן וַעֲצָרָֽה׃

i18n.en: Bring no more worthless meal-offerings; incense is an abomination to me. New moon and sabbath, the calling of convocation — I cannot bear iniquity with solemn assembly.
i18n.he: לֹ֣א תוֹסִ֗יפוּ הָבִיא֙ מִנְחַת־שָׁ֔וְא קְטֹ֧רֶת תּוֹעֵבָ֛ה הִ֖יא לִ֑י חֹ֤דֶשׁ וְשַׁבָּת֙ קְרֹ֣א מִקְרָ֔א לֹא־אוּכַ֥ל אָ֖וֶן וַעֲצָרָֽה׃

notes.official: Three points. (1) *minḥaṯ-šāwʾ* “worthless meal-offerings”: *minḥāh* in this list of offerings is the grain offering, “meal-offering,” under the cultic-list clause of the central `qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus` entry (ASV “vain oblations”). (2) *qᵉṭōreṯ tôʿēḇāh hîʾ lî* “incense is an abomination to me” (ASV; central `toevah-abomination-cross-corpus-keyword`). The noun can also mean the smoke of a burnt sacrifice, and the line follows the usual sense. (3) *ʾāwen waʿăṣārāh* “iniquity with solemn assembly” is MT. The LXX, *nēsteian kai argian* “fasting and rest,” reflects *ṣôm* “fast” for *ʾāwen*, and some commentators adopt it. The line keeps MT (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

paragraphs.translit: lōʾ tōsīpū hābīʾ minḥat-šāwəʾ qəṭōret tōʿēbāh hīʾ lī ḥōdeš wəšabbāt qərōʾ miqrāʾ lōʾ-ʾūkal ʾāwen waʿăṣārāh

paragraphs.text: חָדְשֵׁיכֶ֤ם וּמוֹעֲדֵיכֶם֙ שָׂנְאָ֣ה נַפְשִׁ֔י הָי֥וּ עָלַ֖י לָטֹ֑רַח נִלְאֵ֖יתִי נְשֹֽׂא׃

i18n.en: Your new moons and your appointed feasts my soul hates; they have become a burden to me; I am weary of bearing them.
i18n.he: חָדְשֵׁיכֶ֤ם וּמוֹעֲדֵיכֶם֙ שָׂנְאָ֣ה נַפְשִׁ֔י הָי֥וּ עָלַ֖י לָטֹ֑רַח נִלְאֵ֖יתִי נְשֹֽׂא׃

notes.official: *môʿăḏêḵem* “your appointed feasts” (ASV; NRSV and NJPS “your festivals”). Paired with the new moons, *môʿăḏîm* here are the fixed festivals of the cultic year. The central `moadim` entry (“appointed times”) is scoped to the luminaries of Gen 1:14 and is not extended to this festival use (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-1`).

paragraphs.translit: ḥādəšēkem ūmōʿădēkem śānəʾāh napšī hāyū ʿālay lāṭōraḥ nilʾētī nəśōʾ

paragraphs.text: וּבְפָרִשְׂכֶ֣ם כַּפֵּיכֶ֗ם אַעְלִ֤ים עֵינַי֙ מִכֶּ֔ם גַּ֛ם כִּֽי־תַרְבּ֥וּ תְפִלָּ֖ה אֵינֶ֣נִּי שֹׁמֵ֑עַ יְדֵיכֶ֖ם דָּמִ֥ים מָלֵֽאוּ׃

i18n.en: When you spread out your hands, I will hide my eyes from you; even when you multiply prayer, I am not listening; your hands are full of blood.
i18n.he: וּבְפָרִשְׂכֶ֣ם כַּפֵּיכֶ֗ם אַעְלִ֤ים עֵינַי֙ מִכֶּ֔ם גַּ֛ם כִּֽי־תַרְבּ֥וּ תְפִלָּ֖ה אֵינֶ֣נִּי שֹׁמֵ֑עַ יְדֵיכֶ֖ם דָּמִ֥ים מָלֵֽאוּ׃

paragraphs.translit: ūbəpāriśkem kappēkem ʾaʿlīm ʿēnay mikkem gam kī-tarbū təpillāh ʾēnennī šōmēaʿ yədēkem dāmīm mālēʾū

paragraphs.text: רַחֲצוּ֙ הִזַּכּ֔וּ הָסִ֛ירוּ רֹ֥עַ מַעַלְלֵיכֶ֖ם מִנֶּ֣גֶד עֵינָ֑י חִדְל֖וּ הָרֵֽעַ׃

i18n.en: Wash yourselves, make yourselves clean; remove the evil of your deeds from before my eyes; cease to do evil;
i18n.he: רַחֲצוּ֙ הִזַּכּ֔וּ הָסִ֛ירוּ רֹ֥עַ מַעַלְלֵיכֶ֖ם מִנֶּ֣גֶד עֵינָ֑י חִדְל֖וּ הָרֵֽעַ׃

paragraphs.translit: raḥăṣū hizzakkū hāsīrū rōaʿ maʿallēkem minneged ʿēnāy ḥidlū hārēaʿ

paragraphs.text: לִמְד֥וּ הֵיטֵ֛ב דִּרְשׁ֥וּ מִשְׁפָּ֖ט אַשְּׁר֣וּ חָמ֑וֹץ שִׁפְט֣וּ יָת֔וֹם רִ֖יבוּ אַלְמָנָֽה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: learn to do good; seek justice, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.
i18n.he: לִמְד֥וּ הֵיטֵ֛ב דִּרְשׁ֥וּ מִשְׁפָּ֖ט אַשְּׁר֣וּ חָמ֑וֹץ שִׁפְט֣וּ יָת֔וֹם רִ֖יבוּ אַלְמָנָֽה׃ (ס)

notes.official: *ʾaššᵉrû ḥāmôṣ* “relieve the oppressed”: *ḥāmôṣ* occurs only here. The LXX (*rhysasthe adikoumenon* “rescue the wronged”) and the Vulgate (*subvenite oppresso*) take it as passive, as do ASV, NRSV and NJPS. The noun pattern can also be active, “the ruthless one” (BDB), and with *ʾiššēr* in the sense “set right” that gives “correct the oppressor,” a reading adopted by some modern versions (RSV “correct oppression”). The line follows the ancient versions (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-1`).

paragraphs.translit: limdū hēṭēb diršū mišpāṭ ʾaššərū ḥāmōṣ šipṭū yātōm rībū ʾalmānāh (s)

paragraphs.text: לְכוּ־נָ֛א וְנִוָּֽכְחָ֖ה יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה אִם־יִֽהְי֨וּ חֲטָאֵיכֶ֤ם כַּשָּׁנִים֙ כַּשֶּׁ֣לֶג יַלְבִּ֔ינוּ אִם־יַאְדִּ֥ימוּ כַתּוֹלָ֖ע כַּצֶּ֥מֶר יִהְיֽוּ׃

i18n.en: Come now, and let us reason together, says YHWH: though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be white as snow; though they are red like crimson, they shall become like wool.
i18n.he: לְכוּ־נָ֛א וְנִוָּֽכְחָ֖ה יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה אִם־יִֽהְי֨וּ חֲטָאֵיכֶ֤ם כַּשָּׁנִים֙ כַּשֶּׁ֣לֶג יַלְבִּ֔ינוּ אִם־יַאְדִּ֥ימוּ כַתּוֹלָ֖ע כַּצֶּ֥מֶר יִהְיֽוּ׃

notes.official: *lᵉḵû-nāʾ wᵉniwwāḵᵉḥāh* “Come now, and let us reason together” (ASV). The Niphal of *ykḥ* belongs to the language of the law court: to argue a case or settle a dispute (HALOT; NRSV “let us argue it out”; NJPS “let us reach an understanding”). It continues the lawsuit opened in v. 2. The two conditional clauses are read as promises, as in ASV and NJPS. Several commentators read them as rhetorical questions in the context of the indictment (“though your sins are like scarlet, shall they be white as snow?”). The Hebrew has no question marker, and the line keeps the statement form (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-1`).

paragraphs.translit: ləkū-nāʾ wəniwwākəḥāh yōʾmar YHWH ʾim-yihyū ḥăṭāʾēkem kaššānīm kaššeleg yalbīnū ʾim-yaʾdīmū kattōlāʿ kaṣṣemer yihyū

paragraphs.text: אִם־תֹּאב֖וּ וּשְׁמַעְתֶּ֑ם ט֥וּב הָאָ֖רֶץ תֹּאכֵֽלוּ׃

i18n.en: If you are willing and obey, you shall eat the good of the land;
i18n.he: אִם־תֹּאב֖וּ וּשְׁמַעְתֶּ֑ם ט֥וּב הָאָ֖רֶץ תֹּאכֵֽלוּ׃

paragraphs.translit: ʾim-tōʾbū ūšəmaʿtem ṭūb hāʾāreṣ tōʾkēlū

paragraphs.text: וְאִם־תְּמָאֲנ֖וּ וּמְרִיתֶ֑ם חֶ֣רֶב תְּאֻכְּל֔וּ כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר׃ (ס)

i18n.en: but if you refuse and rebel, you shall be devoured by the sword; for the mouth of YHWH has spoken.
i18n.he: וְאִם־תְּמָאֲנ֖וּ וּמְרִיתֶ֑ם חֶ֣רֶב תְּאֻכְּל֔וּ כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר׃ (ס)

paragraphs.translit: wəʾim-təmāʾănū ūmərītem ḥereb təʾukkəlū kī pī YHWH dibbēr (s)

paragraphs.text: אֵיכָה֙ הָיְתָ֣ה לְזוֹנָ֔ה קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָ֑ה מְלֵאֲתִ֣י מִשְׁפָּ֗ט צֶ֛דֶק יָלִ֥ין בָּ֖הּ וְעַתָּ֥ה מְרַצְּחִֽים׃

i18n.en: How the faithful city has become a prostitute! She was full of justice; righteousness lodged in her — but now murderers.
i18n.he: אֵיכָה֙ הָיְתָ֣ה לְזוֹנָ֔ה קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָ֑ה מְלֵאֲתִ֣י מִשְׁפָּ֗ט צֶ֛דֶק יָלִ֥ין בָּ֖הּ וְעַתָּ֥ה מְרַצְּחִֽים׃

notes.official: *ʾêḵāh* “How” is the opening cry of the funeral lament (compare Lam 1:1). *zônāh* is “prostitute” under the central `zonah-prostitute-status-vocabulary-cross-corpus` entry; the image of the city as an unfaithful wife is used by Hosea, Jeremiah and Ezekiel as well. The *qiryāh neʾĕmānāh* “faithful city” returns at v. 26, framing the unit vv. 21–26.

paragraphs.translit: ʾēkāh hāyətāh ləzōnāh qiryāh neʾĕmānāh məlēʾătī mišpāṭ ṣedeq yālīn bāh wəʿattāh məraṣṣəḥīm

paragraphs.text: כַּסְפֵּ֖ךְ הָיָ֣ה לְסִיגִ֑ים סָבְאֵ֖ךְ מָה֥וּל בַּמָּֽיִם׃

i18n.en: Your silver has become dross, your wine diluted with water.
i18n.he: כַּסְפֵּ֖ךְ הָיָ֣ה לְסִיגִ֑ים סָבְאֵ֖ךְ מָה֥וּל בַּמָּֽיִם׃

paragraphs.translit: kaspēk hāyāh ləsīgīm sābəʾēk māhūl bammāyim

paragraphs.text: שָׂרַ֣יִךְ סוֹרְרִ֗ים וְחַבְרֵי֙ גַּנָּבִ֔ים כֻּלּוֹ֙ אֹהֵ֣ב שֹׁ֔חַד וְרֹדֵ֖ף שַׁלְמֹנִ֑ים יָתוֹם֙ לֹ֣א יִשְׁפֹּ֔טוּ וְרִ֥יב אַלְמָנָ֖ה לֹֽא־יָב֥וֹא אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃ (פ)

i18n.en: Your princes are rebels and companions of thieves; every one loves a bribe and runs after gifts. They do not judge the fatherless, and the widow's cause does not come to them.
i18n.he: שָׂרַ֣יִךְ סוֹרְרִ֗ים וְחַבְרֵי֙ גַּנָּבִ֔ים כֻּלּוֹ֙ אֹהֵ֣ב שֹׁ֔חַד וְרֹדֵ֖ף שַׁלְמֹנִ֑ים יָתוֹם֙ לֹ֣א יִשְׁפֹּ֔טוּ וְרִ֥יב אַלְמָנָ֖ה לֹֽא־יָב֥וֹא אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃ (פ)

paragraphs.translit: śārayik sōrərīm wəḥabrē gannābīm kullō ʾōhēb šōḥad wərōdēp šalmōnīm yātōm lōʾ yišpōṭū wərīb ʾalmānāh lōʾ-yābōʾ ʾălēhem (p)

paragraphs.text: לָכֵ֗ן נְאֻ֤ם הָֽאָדוֹן֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת אֲבִ֖יר יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ה֚וֹי אֶנָּחֵ֣ם מִצָּרַ֔י וְאִנָּקְמָ֖ה מֵאוֹיְבָֽי׃

i18n.en: Therefore says the Sovereign, YHWH of hosts, the Mighty One of Israel: Woe! I will ease myself of my adversaries, and avenge myself on my enemies.
i18n.he: לָכֵ֗ן נְאֻ֤ם הָֽאָדוֹן֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת אֲבִ֖יר יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ה֚וֹי אֶנָּחֵ֣ם מִצָּרַ֔י וְאִנָּקְמָ֖ה מֵאוֹיְבָֽי׃

notes.official: *hā-ʾāḏôn* “the Sovereign” is the noun *ʾāḏôn* “lord, master” with the article, not the title *ʾăḏōnāy* rendered “the Lord” at 6:1 and elsewhere (overlay `adonai-standalone-title-isaiah`). The line follows NRSV and NJPS “the Sovereign,” so that the two Hebrew forms keep distinct English; ASV has “the Lord” for both. The same articular title stands before “YHWH of hosts” at 3:1, 10:16, 10:33 and 19:4 (overlay `ha-adon-articular-title-isaiah`). *ʾăḇîr yiśrāʾēl* “the Mighty One of Israel” is the Isaiah form of the old title “the Mighty One of Jacob” (Gen 49:24; Ps 132:2, 5; central `avir-yaaqov-mighty-one-of-yaaqov-divine-title-cross-corpus`). *hôy* is “Woe” (overlay `hoy-woe-isaiah`); here it introduces a threat against YHWH’s adversaries. *ʾennāḥēm miṣṣāray* “I will ease myself of my adversaries” (ASV): the Niphal of *nḥm* with *min* means to get relief from, here by vengeance (BDB; NJPS “I will get satisfaction from my foes”) (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-1`).

paragraphs.translit: lākēn nəʾum hāʾādōn YHWH ṣəbāʾōt ʾăbīr yiśrāʾēl hōy ʾennāḥēm miṣṣāray wəʾinnāqəmāh mēʾōyəbāy

paragraphs.text: וְאָשִׁ֤יבָה יָדִי֙ עָלַ֔יִךְ וְאֶצְרֹ֥ף כַּבֹּ֖ר סִיגָ֑יִךְ וְאָסִ֖ירָה כָּל־בְּדִילָֽיִךְ׃

i18n.en: And I will turn my hand against you, and thoroughly smelt away your dross, and remove all your tin.
i18n.he: וְאָשִׁ֤יבָה יָדִי֙ עָלַ֔יִךְ וְאֶצְרֹ֥ף כַּבֹּ֖ר סִיגָ֑יִךְ וְאָסִ֖ירָה כָּל־בְּדִילָֽיִךְ׃

notes.official: *wᵉʾeṣrōp̄ kabbōr sîḡāyiḵ* “and thoroughly smelt away your dross” follows ASV, which derives *bōr* from the noun “cleanness” (2 Sam 22:21, 25): “to purity,” hence “thoroughly.” NRSV and NJPS take *bōr* as “lye, potash” (Job 9:30; HALOT), a flux used in refining: “smelt away your dross as with lye.” The conjecture *bakkûr* “in the furnace” changes the text and is not adopted. *bᵉḏîlāyiḵ* is “your tin” (ASV; Num 31:22; Ezek 22:18, 20), the base metal mixed into silver; NRSV and NJPS have “alloy.” The refining image takes up v. 22, “your silver has become dross” (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-1`).

paragraphs.translit: wəʾāšībāh yādī ʿālayik wəʾeṣrōp kabbōr sīgāyik wəʾāsīrāh kol-bədīlāyik

paragraphs.text: וְאָשִׁ֤יבָה שֹׁפְטַ֙יִךְ֙ כְּבָרִ֣אשֹׁנָ֔ה וְיֹעֲצַ֖יִךְ כְּבַתְּחִלָּ֑ה אַחֲרֵי־כֵ֗ן יִקָּ֤רֵא לָךְ֙ עִ֣יר הַצֶּ֔דֶק קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָֽה׃

i18n.en: And I will restore your judges as at the first, and your counselors as at the beginning; afterward you shall be called the city of righteousness, a faithful city.
i18n.he: וְאָשִׁ֤יבָה שֹׁפְטַ֙יִךְ֙ כְּבָרִ֣אשֹׁנָ֔ה וְיֹעֲצַ֖יִךְ כְּבַתְּחִלָּ֑ה אַחֲרֵי־כֵ֗ן יִקָּ֤רֵא לָךְ֙ עִ֣יר הַצֶּ֔דֶק קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָֽה׃

paragraphs.translit: wəʾāšībāh šōpəṭayik kəbāriʾšōnāh wəyōʿăṣayik kəbattəḥillāh ʾaḥărē-kēn yiqqārēʾ lāk ʿīr haṣṣedeq qiryāh neʾĕmānāh

paragraphs.text: צִיּ֖וֹן בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט תִּפָּדֶ֑ה וְשָׁבֶ֖יהָ בִּצְדָקָֽה׃

i18n.en: Zion shall be redeemed by justice, and those of her who return, by righteousness.
i18n.he: צִיּ֖וֹן בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט תִּפָּדֶ֑ה וְשָׁבֶ֖יהָ בִּצְדָקָֽה׃

notes.official: *wᵉšāḇêhā* “and those of her who return” keeps the ambiguity of the Hebrew participle of *šûḇ*: those who turn back to YHWH (ASV “her converts”; NJPS “her repentant ones”) or those who come back to the city. The LXX, *hē aichmalōsia autēs* “her captivity,” reflects a different vocalisation, *šᵉḇyāh* (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-1`).

paragraphs.translit: ṣiyyōn bəmišpāṭ tippādeh wəšābēhā biṣdāqāh

paragraphs.text: וְשֶׁ֧בֶר פֹּשְׁעִ֛ים וְחַטָּאִ֖ים יַחְדָּ֑ו וְעֹזְבֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה יִכְלֽוּ׃

i18n.en: But the destruction of transgressors and sinners shall be together, and those who forsake YHWH shall be consumed.
i18n.he: וְשֶׁ֧בֶר פֹּשְׁעִ֛ים וְחַטָּאִ֖ים יַחְדָּ֑ו וְעֹזְבֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה יִכְלֽוּ׃

notes.official: *pōšʿîm* “transgressors” (ASV; NRSV and NJPS “rebels”). The chapter has three other words for rebellion, *mārāh* (v. 20), *sārar* (v. 23) and *sārāh* (v. 5). “Transgressors” keeps *pšʿ* distinct in English from *sôrᵉrîm* “rebels” in v. 23 (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-1`).

paragraphs.translit: wəšeber pōšəʿīm wəḥaṭṭāʾīm yaḥdāw wəʿōzəbē YHWH yiklū

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י יֵבֹ֔שׁוּ מֵאֵילִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר חֲמַדְתֶּ֑ם וְתַ֨חְפְּר֔וּ מֵהַגַּנּ֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּחַרְתֶּֽם׃

i18n.en: For they shall be ashamed of the terebinths that you desired, and you shall blush for the gardens that you have chosen.
i18n.he: כִּ֣י יֵבֹ֔שׁוּ מֵאֵילִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר חֲמַדְתֶּ֑ם וְתַ֨חְפְּר֔וּ מֵהַגַּנּ֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּחַרְתֶּֽם׃

notes.official: Two points. (1) *yēḇōšû* “they shall be ashamed” is third person, and *ḥămaḏtem* “you desired” is second person. The person shift is MT and is kept, as in ASV (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). NRSV renders the second person throughout (“you shall be ashamed”). (2) *ʾêlîm* are large trees, terebinths. The line has “terebinths,” as in NJPS, to agree with *ʾēlāh* “terebinth” at 6:13, where the overlay keeps *ʾēlāh* distinct from *ʾallôn* “oak” (overlay `elah-terebinth-allon-oak-isaiah`; ASV “oaks”). The trees and *gannôṯ* “gardens” are sites of cult outside the Temple; compare 65:3, 66:17, and Hos 4:13.

paragraphs.translit: kī yēbōšū mēʾēlīm ʾăšer ḥămadtem wətaḥpərū mēhaggannōt ʾăšer bəḥartem

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י תִֽהְי֔וּ כְּאֵלָ֖ה נֹבֶ֣לֶת עָלֶ֑הָ וּֽכְגַנָּ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־מַ֖יִם אֵ֥ין לָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: For you shall be like a terebinth whose leaf withers, and like a garden that has no water.
i18n.he: כִּ֣י תִֽהְי֔וּ כְּאֵלָ֖ה נֹבֶ֣לֶת עָלֶ֑הָ וּֽכְגַנָּ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־מַ֖יִם אֵ֥ין לָֽהּ׃

notes.official: *kᵉʾēlāh nōḇeleṯ ʿālehā* “like a terebinth whose leaf withers”: *ʾēlāh* is “terebinth,” as at 6:13 (overlay `elah-terebinth-allon-oak-isaiah`; ASV “an oak”). The verse turns the trees and gardens of v. 29 into the image of the people’s own fate.

paragraphs.translit: kī tihyū kəʾēlāh nōbelet ʿālehā ūkəgannāh ʾăšer-mayim ʾēn lāh

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֤ה הֶחָסֹן֙ לִנְעֹ֔רֶת וּפֹעֲל֖וֹ לְנִיצ֑וֹץ וּבָעֲר֧וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֛ם יַחְדָּ֖ו וְאֵ֥ין מְכַבֶּֽה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And the strong shall become tinder, and its maker a spark; and both of them shall burn together, with none to quench them.
i18n.he: וְהָיָ֤ה הֶחָסֹן֙ לִנְעֹ֔רֶת וּפֹעֲל֖וֹ לְנִיצ֑וֹץ וּבָעֲר֧וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֛ם יַחְדָּ֖ו וְאֵ֥ין מְכַבֶּֽה׃ (ס)

notes.official: *hā-ḥāsōn* “the strong” occurs elsewhere only at Amos 2:9, “strong as the oaks.” *nᵉʿōreṯ* is the coarse fibre of flax, which catches fire at once (Judg 16:9); the line has “tinder” (NRSV, NJPS) for ASV “tow.” *ûp̄ōʿălô* is “and its maker.” The Masoretic vowels (holem on *pe*, hatef patah on *ʿayin*) are those of the Qal participle *pōʿēl* with suffix: compare Job 36:3 *lᵉp̄ōʿălî* “to my Maker.” The noun *pōʿal* with the suffix is pointed *pāʿŏlô* (Jer 22:13; Prov 20:11). ASV and NRSV have “and his work,” which reads the noun and so presupposes that repointing. The line follows the pointed text, as at 1:12 (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). Read with the pointing, the verse is about the strong one and the one who made it, perhaps the idol and its maker (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-1`).

paragraphs.translit: wəhāyāh heḥāsōn linʿōret ūpōʿălō lənīṣōṣ ūbāʿărū šənēhem yaḥdāw wəʾēn məkabbeh (s)
